title: रससूत्रको व्याख्याका मतान्तरहरु र यसको तात्पर्य {Contradictions in the interpretation of Rasasutra and its meaning}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख पूर्र्वीय साहित्यशास्त्रमा सर्वाधिक चिन्तन र बहस भएको भरतमुनिले प्रतिपादन गरेको रससूत्रको मतान्तर सहितको विवेचनामा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । भरतमुनिले विभाव, अनुभाव र व्यभिचारी भावको संयोगबाट रस निष्पत्ति हुन्छ भनी प्रस्तुत गरेको रससूत्रलाई उनका उत्तरवर्र्ती भट्टलोल्लट, श्रीशंकुक,भट्टनायक र अभिनवगुप्त जस्ता रस चिन्तकहरुले व्याख्या गरे । यी व्याख्याताका व्याख्या आआफ्ना मतानुसारी छन् । तिनमा मतैक्य छैन। भरतले आफ्नो रससूत्रमा रस के हो ? यसको स्वरुप कस्तो हुन्छ ? भन्ने उल्लेख नगरी रस कसरी उत्पन्नहुन्छ भन्ने बारेमा मात्र उल्लेख गरेका छन् । यही आधारमा टेकेर उत्तरवर्र्ती आचार्यहरु मध्ये भट्टलोल्लटले रस उत्पत्ति हुने, श्रीशंकुकले रस अनुमिति हुने, भट्टनायकले भुक्ति हुने र अभिनवगुप्तले अभिव्यक्ति हुने भनी व्याख्या गरेका छन् । यी उत्तरवर्र्ती आचार्यहरूको व्याख्या मूलतः रससूत्रमा प्रयुक्त “संयोगात्” र “निष्पत्ति” दुई शब्दको व्याख्यामा आधारित रहेर आआफ्ना दार्शनिक चेतको मूल्यसमेत प्रतिबिम्बित हुने गरी आएका छन् । यीव्याख्यालाई चिन्तन र व्यावहारिकताका कसीमा राखेर हेर्दा पाठकले काव्य नाटक वा साहित्यको अध्ययन आनन्दप्राप्त गर्नका लागि गर्ने र त्यो आनन्द मुख्य विषयको साधारणीकरण भई व्यष्टिबाट समष्टिमा गई रसास्वादनप्राप्त गर्दछ भन्ने देखिन्छ। रससूत्रमा आएका संयोग र निष्पत्ति शब्दलाई लिएर चारजनाले प्रस्तुत गरेको व्याख्याको अर्थ के हो र तीमध्ये सबैभन्दा व्यावहारिक वा उपयुक्त अर्थ कुन हुनसक्छ भन्ने विषयलाई समेत प्रस्तुत गरिएकोछ । साथै रस केमा रहन्छ र त्यो रसको आस्वाद कसलाई प्राप्त हुन्छ भन्ने प्रश्न एकातिर रहिरहन्छ भने अर्कोतिरसंयोग र निष्पत्तिको मुख्यार्थ के हो भन्ने विषयमा फरक चर्चा परिचर्चा उत्पन्न हुन्छ र यसले रसनिष्पत्ति सिद्धान्तग्रहण गर्न पुग्दछ । यही रसनिष्पत्ति सिद्धान्तको चर्चा यसमा गरिएको छ । विशेष गरी चारवटा आचार्यकाव्याख्यालाई आधार मानेर तत्सम्बन्धी मतमतान्तर र व्याख्याको आशयलाई यसमा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ l {The present article focuses on the most thought-provoking and debated discourses in Eastern literature, including the dissertation of Rasasutra. The Rasasutra presented by Bharat Muni that juice is derived from the coincidence of perception, experience and adulterous emotion was interpreted by his successors like Bhattalollat, Srishankuk, Bhattanayak and Abhinav Gupta. The interpretations of these lecturers are according to their own opinions. He has no consensus. What is the juice in Bharat's Rasasutra?  What does it look like? They have only mentioned how the juice is produced without mentioning it. On this basis, Bhattalollat, one of the later Acharyas, has explained that juice originates, Sreesanku gives juice, Bhattanayaka gives bhukti, and Abhinav Gupta gives expression. The interpretation of these later Acharyas is based on the interpretation of the two words "coincidence" and "decision" used in the Rasasutra and reflects the value of their philosophical consciousness. Putting these interpretations in the context of contemplation and practicality, it seems that the reader enjoys the study of poetic drama or literature for the sake of enjoyment, and that enjoyment becomes a generalization of the main subject and goes from individual to collective. What is the meaning of the explanation given by the four of them regarding the word coincidence and decision in Rasasutra and also what is the most practical or suitable meaning among them? At the same time, the question remains as to what the juice is and who gets the taste of that juice, on the one hand, and on the other hand, what is the main purpose of coincidence and decision? This is the principle of rationality discussed in it. In particular, based on the four Acharya interpretations, the meaning of the dissent and interpretation is presented in it.}
american_english: The present article focuses on the discussion, along with differences of opinion, of the Rasasutra formulated by Bharata Muni, which has been the subject of the greatest reflection and debate in Eastern poetics. The Rasasutra presented by Bharata Muni stating that rasa is produced from the conjunction of vibhava [determinant], anubhava [consequent], and vyabhichari bhava [transitory state] was interpreted by later rasa theorists such as Bhatta Lollata, Sri Shankuka, Bhatta Nayaka, and Abhinavagupta. The interpretations of these commentators accord with their respective opinions. There is no consensus among them. In his Rasasutra, without mentioning what is rasa? or what is its nature like?, Bharata has only mentioned how rasa is produced. Relying on this very premise, among the subsequent acharyas, Bhatta Lollata interpreted that rasa is produced, Sri Shankuka that rasa is inferred, Bhatta Nayaka that it is experienced, and Abhinavagupta that it is expressed. The interpretations of these subsequent acharyas are fundamentally based on the interpretation of the two words "samyogat" and "nishpatti" used in the Rasasutra, emerging in such a way that the values of their respective philosophical consciousness are also reflected. When examining these interpretations against the touchstone of reflection and practicality, it is seen that a reader undertakes the study of poetry, drama, or literature to attain joy, and that joy, through the universalization of the primary subject, moves from the individual to the collective, thereby attaining the relish of rasa. What the interpretations presented by the four thinkers regarding the words samyoga and nishpatti appearing in the Rasasutra mean, and which among them might be the most practical or appropriate meaning, is also presented. Moreover, while on the one hand the question persists as to what rasa resides in and who attains the relish of that rasa, on the other hand different discussions arise regarding what the primary meaning of samyoga and nishpatti is, and this leads to the adoption of the theory of rasa realization. It is this very theory of rasa realization that is discussed here. Basing itself particularly on the interpretations of the four acharyas, the related differences of opinion and the import of the interpretations are presented in this article.
